description: Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly above 0.0005 are included; a rate of exactly 0.0005 is excluded.

c.request: For the high-rebate fee records, using 0.0005 on the maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) as the cutoff, what are the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`)? Return one row with these two values in that order, unrounded, ignoring missing values (each value is empty if there is nothing to aggregate). Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly above 0.0005 are included; a rate of exactly 0.0005 is excluded.
c.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS average_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

b.request: For fee records with `rebrate > 0.0005`, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` and `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, in that order, without rounding; ignore NULL values, and return NULL for an aggregate with no values.
b.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal), AVG(feerate - rebrate) FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
b.raw: For fee records with `rebrate > 0.0005`, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` and `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, in that order, without rounding; ignore NULL values, and return NULL for an aggregate with no values.

a.request: Across all fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is strictly greater than 0.0005, what are the total rebate (the sum of `rebtotal`) and the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`)? Return one row with these two values in that order, unrounded, ignoring missing values (each value is empty if there is nothing to aggregate).
a.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS average_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

d.request: For fee records where `rebrate` > 0.0005, return one row containing `SUM(rebtotal)` followed by `AVG(feerate - rebrate)`, unrounded, with missing values ignored and each aggregate empty if it has no values.
d.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal), AVG(feerate - rebrate) FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
